events.text: Sir John Pawlett leased most of Westover to Theodorick Bland for £170.

evidence.quote: demised most of Westover Plantation in 1665 to Theodorick Bland of Westover for £170

events.text: Theodorick and Richard Bland conveyed 1,200 acres to William Byrd I.

evidence.quote: conveyed 1,200 acres of the property to William Byrd I in 1688

events.text: Mansion thought built by William Byrd II, c. 1730; later disputed.

evidence.quote: William Byrd II , the founder of Richmond , was thought to have built the mansion c . 1730

events.text: Westover sold out of the Byrd family after the widow's death.

evidence.quote: After the death of William Byrd IIIs widow in 1814 , Westover was sold out of the Byrd family

events.text: House designated a National Historic Landmark.

evidence.quote: This date was part of the 1960 designation of the house as a National Historic Landmark
The plantation has been designated as a National Historic Landmark in the United States

events.label: damage
events.text: Site damaged by Hurricane Isabel; riverbank and trees eroded.

evidence.quote: The site was damaged by Hurricane Isabel in 2003

undated_mentions: Mansion probably built and first occupied by William Byrd III, dated by dendrochronology to the 1750s
Westover used as headquarters of the Union Fifth Corps during the American Civil War; one wing burned
Richard Teller Crane II acquired Westover in the early 20th century and restored the mansion and grounds
Plantation was one of the sites of Charles City County courts in the early years of the Virginia colony
Planters shifted from tobacco to mixed crops in the 19th century
Augustus Harrison Drewry rebuilt the burned wing, connected dependencies and enlarged the dining room
